description_good_justification: The README says in its first lines what module-kit is: the NovaTrail module format in code, the one Go library that holds the format's semantics — checking a module, building its package and the module index, comparing versions, the open view, the check kinds, the leak check and the Starlark sandbox — and the authors' CLI on top of it. https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit#readme
interact_justification: The README says how to obtain module-kit (a release binary, checked before its first run, or the Go module at a tag), how to give feedback (GitHub issues) and how to contribute (its Contributing section and the organization's CONTRIBUTING.md). https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit#contributing
contribution_justification: Changes come as GitHub pull requests: an issue first, then a pull request whose every commit is signed off under the Developer Certificate of Origin. The branch main takes changes only through pull requests whose checks pass. The process is in the organization's CONTRIBUTING.md, which GitHub shows for this repository, and the organization's issue forms and pull request template, which GitHub shows too, ask for what it needs: https://github.com/altnovatrail/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md lists what every contribution keeps to (no learners' data, no secrets, the devcontainer, licenses compatible with Apache-2.0, a DCO sign-off) and points to the rules every NovaTrail repository shares, RULES.md, which include the rule on tests: https://github.com/altnovatrail/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md and https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/blob/main/RULES.md
floss_license_justification: Apache-2.0, an OSI-approved license, covers the code and the documents. https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit/blob/main/LICENSE
floss_license_osi_justification: Apache-2.0 is approved by the OSI.
license_location_justification: The license is the top-level file LICENSE: https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit/blob/main/LICENSE
documentation_basics_justification: The README says what module-kit does, how to take and verify a release binary or the Go module, how to work on it (open the repository in its devcontainer) and how to run the checks and tests. RULES.md says what keeps the work safe: everything inside the devcontainer, exact versions checked against their sums, no secrets and no learners' data in the repository. https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit#readme
documentation_interface_justification: The library's external interface is its exported Go API, and every package and exported name has a doc comment, which pkg.go.dev renders: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit. The CLI prints the form of every command when called with none, and its doc comment says what each command reads and writes and what each exit status means: 0 accepted, 1 refused by the rules of the format with their IDs, 2 could not do its work. https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit/blob/main/cmd/module-kit/main.go
sites_https_justification: The project's only site is its GitHub repository, served over HTTPS: https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests: searchable, addressable by URL, open to anyone with a GitHub account, and nothing to install. https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit/issues
english_justification: The README, CLAUDE.md, the code, its comments and the CLI's messages are in English, and issues and pull requests are accepted in English or Russian. The descriptive documents under docs/ and the work plan are in Russian, the author's working language.
maintained_justification: Under active development: see the commits and the releases. https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit/releases
repo_public_justification: A public git repository on GitHub: https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit
repo_track_justification: Git records what changed, who changed it and when, and every commit of a pull request is signed off under the DCO.
repo_interim_justification: Every pull request, its branch and its commits are public before they reach main and a release.
repo_distributed_justification: The repository is git, hosted on GitHub.
version_unique_justification: Every release has a unique version vX.Y.Z, tagged on its commit. The release workflow numbers it, and nobody tags by hand; releases are immutable, and a ruleset forbids moving or deleting a tag v*. https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml
version_semver_justification: Versions are MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH: each release is the next patch of the current line. The line 0.1 held the steps of the first epic of code; the line 0.2, from v0.2.0, is the first that others take, and a change that breaks those who take it starts a new line.
version_tags_justification: Each release is the git tag vX.Y.Z, which the release workflow creates together with the release; the Go module takes the same tag as its version.
release_notes_justification: A release follows every merge to main that changes what a release is built from, and its notes on GitHub list the pull request it brings, linked to the pull request's description: an English summary of what changed and why. https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit/releases
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability of module-kit has been fixed in any release. If one is, its release notes will name it and link its GitHub security advisory.
report_process_justification: Bugs are reported as GitHub issues, through the bug report form that GitHub shows for every repository of the organization: it asks what happened, what was expected, how to reproduce it on synthetic data and in which commit, release or tag. https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit/issues/new/choose
report_tracker_justification: GitHub issues track individual reports. The project's own planned work is in its work plan, RUN.md.
report_responses_justification: No bug report has been submitted yet; the maintainer answers each report in its issue.
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement request has been submitted yet; the maintainer answers each request in its issue.
report_archive_justification: GitHub issues are public, permanent and searchable: https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: The security policy, which every repository of the organization shares, says how to report a vulnerability: privately, through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting. https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit/security/policy
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled: a report goes over HTTPS to the maintainers and opens a draft advisory that only they and the reporter see. https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability has been reported in the last six months.
build_justification: `just build` builds the CLI with the go command, and `just release-files <version>` builds a release's files: the CLI for six platforms without cgo, with -trimpath and no VCS stamp, so that the build is reproducible, the licenses of the modules it is built from and SHA256SUMS. The release builds them in the toolchain stage of .devcontainer/Dockerfile, from a base image pinned by digest and tools pinned by version and SHA-256. https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit/blob/main/justfile
build_common_tools_justification: The go command builds, vets and tests the code, with govulncheck and go-licenses run by it, Docker builds the environment, and just runs every recipe.
build_floss_tools_justification: All FLOSS: Go (BSD-3-Clause), Docker Engine (Apache-2.0), just (CC0-1.0), govulncheck (BSD-3-Clause), go-licenses (Apache-2.0), and cosign (Apache-2.0), which signs the release's files.
test_justification: An automated test suite in this repository, under Apache-2.0, run by the go command: the tests of every package, among them one that runs every example and test vector of the module format and of the observation against the library and skips none. `just ci-test` runs them all; the README says so, and CI runs them on every pull request and on main: https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_invocation_justification: `just ci-test` runs every test with the race detector, by `go test ./...`, the standard way for Go; the README names it.
test_most_justification: On 2026-11-06 the tests covered 97.96% of the lines of the code on main (e9acd75), as Codecov counts them: https://app.codecov.io/gh/altnovatrail/module-kit
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs every check and every test on each pull request and on each commit to main, and main takes a pull request only when they pass. CI also runs each binary of a release on a runner of its own system.
test_policy_justification: RULES.md, the rules every NovaTrail repository shares: code comes with its tests, so a pull request that adds or changes what code does adds or changes the tests of its automated suite. A pull request merges only when at least 90% of its changed lines are covered (codecov/patch, a required check), and code that reads foreign input comes with a fuzz test. https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/blob/main/RULES.md
tests_are_added_justification: The latest major changes came with their tests: the command open, with tests over every test vector of packages and of templates and its fuzz test (https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit/pull/59); the commands index and diff, over every test vector of the index and of versions (#56); the commands check and build (#54).
tests_documented_added_justification: The rule on tests is in RULES.md, which the organization's CONTRIBUTING.md names as the rules every contribution follows, and the pull request template that GitHub shows for every repository of the organization asks for it: code comes with its tests. https://github.com/altnovatrail/.github/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md
warnings_justification: gofmt and `go vet` check the Go code on every pull request, as `just ci-lint` runs them in the required check Go / lint, and the bash scripts run with `set -euo pipefail`. SonarCloud analyses the code on every pull request, and its quality gate is a required check. https://sonarcloud.io/summary/new_code?id=altnovatrail_module-kit
warnings_fixed_justification: A finding of SonarCloud or CodeQL is fixed in code before the next task starts; marking one false is a last resort, with the reason written down. SonarCloud's current findings are public: https://sonarcloud.io/project/issues?id=altnovatrail_module-kit
warnings_strict_justification: SonarCloud's quality gate holds a merge on any new finding, and the answer to a finding is a change to the code: even findings below the gate, such as shell:S7688 in the script that runs the binaries, were fixed in their pull request (#57).
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer designs for least privilege, fail-safe defaults and a small attack surface. The library does no input or output and no network: files come to it as bytes or an fs.FS, and it trusts a package only by the chain of SHA-256 digests from a pinned index, each file held to its digest, its schema and its canonical text. A module is data: its Starlark runs in a sandbox with a limit of steps and a clock, and its YAML is read by an allowlist of what the format takes. The CLI writes a new file or folder through a temporary folder only its owner may read. Every workflow starts with a read-only token, a job gets only the write it needs, the workflows hold no secret, and main has no bypass. The decisions behind these, in Russian, are in https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit/blob/main/docs/decisions.md
know_common_errors_justification: For this kind of software, a reader of untrusted files and a sandbox for untrusted expressions, the maintainer counters: YAML pitfalls, such as implicit types and alias expansion (anchors and aliases are refused, and every value has one JSON form); path traversal (a path of a package or of the output must be a valid path inside its folder); tampering with a package (every file held to its digest); resource exhaustion by a module's Starlark (a limit of steps and a clock; a limit of memory waits for third-party modules, an open debt in RUN.md); malformed input (a fuzz test for each reader of foreign input); supply-chain tampering (actions pinned by commit, downloads checked against pinned SHA-256 sums; Scorecard's Dangerous-Workflow check scores 10); and instructions hidden in data for an AI model (a module is data, never instructions, and a program decides every verdict).
crypto_published_justification: module-kit implements no cryptography. It relies on SHA-256, published and reviewed (FIPS 180-4): the module format names a package by the SHA-256 of its canonical text, and the library reads a package by the chain of those digests. The release signs its files with cosign, keyless, through Sigstore, whose certificates and signatures are ECDSA, also published and reviewed (FIPS 186-5).
crypto_call_justification: It calls Go's crypto/sha256 for the digests, and the shared release workflow calls cosign to sign the release's files; it never implements cryptography itself.
crypto_floss_justification: Go's standard library (BSD-3-Clause) and cosign (Apache-2.0) are FLOSS.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithm is used: SHA-256 only.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No algorithm with known serious weaknesses is used: SHA-256 only, never SHA-1 or MD5.
crypto_pfs_justification: module-kit implements no key agreement and makes no network connection.
crypto_random_justification: module-kit generates no keys or nonces. Its generator of the format's randomness picks instances of task templates and is no cryptographic generator, by design.
delivery_mitm_justification: module-kit is delivered over HTTPS only: the repository, its releases and their files, and its Go module through the Go module proxy, whose checksum database holds each version to its bytes. Releases are immutable, GitHub attests each one with its files, and each file is signed with cosign, its bundle beside it in the release. spec's `just release-verify` checks a file against its bundle and Sigstore's trust root and against everything the certificate names: who signed, at whose call, on which branch and of which commit; NovaTrail's CI checks a binary so before its first run.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is retrieved over HTTP: every SHA-256 sum is pinned in the file next to its version, and every download of the devcontainer is restricted to HTTPS, redirects included (curl --proto =https --proto-redir =https).
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No vulnerability is open: Dependabot has raised no alert, and govulncheck finds none. When govulncheck found two advisories in golang.org/x/text v0.14.0, which a new dependency required, the same pull request raised it to v0.43.0 before it merged (#38).
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Dependabot security updates are on, govulncheck is a required check, and a finding of Scorecard, CodeQL or SonarCloud is fixed before the next task starts.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: gitleaks scans the whole history on every pull request and on main, and GitHub's secret scanning and push protection are on. The workflows hold no secret: coverage goes to Codecov with a short-lived OIDC token.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL, with the security-extended queries, analyses the Go code and every workflow, and SonarCloud analyses the repository, on every pull request and on main. Both are required checks, CodeQL for each of its languages, and a release comes only after CI passes on main.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's security-extended queries and SonarCloud's security rules look for common vulnerabilities, and govulncheck for the known vulnerabilities of the Go vulnerability database in the code and the standard library it reaches (Go / vuln, a required check). SonarCloud found, and the pull request fixed before it merged, a folder made readable to all (go:S2612, #54).
static_analysis_fixed_justification: The ruleset of main holds a merge on any CodeQL alert at error level or of high severity and above, and on SonarCloud's quality gate; every finding is fixed before the next task starts.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every pull request and on every commit to main.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Every reader of foreign input has a fuzz test of Go's own fuzzing — the YAML of a module, a package, an index, an observation, Starlark expressions and programs, pictures, among 22 —, which the task that brings or changes the reader runs for one to ten minutes, and whose seed corpus runs on every pull request. The automated tests run with the race detector and cover 97.96% of the lines.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: module-kit is Go, a memory-safe language, built without cgo, and its code imports no package unsafe.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Go has no assertions to switch on: the code checks its own invariants always, and a broken one is a panic that names it, never a wrong result; the tests check every result they get.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: A failing test fails a required check, and the pull request cannot merge until it passes. Fuzzing found inputs that crashed readers — a number above the range of a double, `1e700`, among them — and each was fixed, with the input kept in the tests, before its pull request merged. No vulnerability has been found this way.
